q: In India executive have the power to legislate by Ordinances. But Legislature shall approve it otherwise the ordinance can exist at most
explanation: The maximum gap between sessions is six months and an ordinance lapses six weeks after reassembly, so its maximum life without approval is six months and six weeks.

notes.text: - **Maximum life = six months + six weeks**: maximum gap between sessions is **six months** (**Art. 85**; States **Art. 174**) + the six-week window – so neither "six months", "three months" nor "indefinitely".

explanation: The Deputy PM is not mentioned in the Constitution; the Cabinet (Art. 352, 44th Amendment), Council of Ministers (Art. 74) and Speaker (Art. 93) are.

q: First Deputy Prime Minister of India was
explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was India's first Deputy Prime Minister (1947-50); Morarji Desai (1967) and Devi Lal (1989) came later, and G.B. Pant never held the post.

q: As per the Indian Constitution, in the Union Council of Ministers,
options: Cabinet Ministers are superior to other ministers
Deputy Ministers are superior to Ministers of State, but lower than Cabinet Ministers in rank a se
Ministers without portfolios are the lowest in rank in the Council of Ministers
explanation: The Constitution creates one Council of Ministers and does not grade its members; the ranks Cabinet Minister / Minister of State / Deputy Minister are conventional, so 'as per the Constitution' all Ministers are equal. Option B is true only by convention; Deputy Ministers rank below Ministers of State, not above.

notes.text: # Appointment (Article 75(1))

- **"The Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President"** – **Art. 75(1)** (not Arts. 32, 70, 74, 79, 356, 348); **other Ministers** are appointed by the President **on the advice of the PM**. The PM is **not elected** by Parliament or the Lok Sabha and is not merely "nominated by the majority party".

q: Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India are correct? i. The Vice President is elected for five years. ii. The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. iii. The Vice President acts as the President only until a new President is elected.
explanation: All three: the VP is elected for five years, is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and on a vacancy acts as President only until a new President is elected (max six months).

notes.text: - **42nd Amendment (1976)** made the advice **binding** on the President; **44th (1978)** added the one-time reconsideration. **Article 74(3) does not exist.** During a National Emergency the advice stays binding.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the office of Vice-President?
options: The Vice-President office is modelled on the lines of the American Vice-President.
The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament.
All doubts and disputes in connection with the election of the Vice-President are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court of India.

If the office of the Vice-President falls vacant due to resignation, removal, death, or any other reason, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha acts as Vice-President until a new Vice-President is elected.
key_text: If the office of the Vice-President falls vacant due to resignation, removal, death, or any other reason, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha acts as Vice-President until a new Vice-President is elected.
explanation: Not correct: (d). The Constitution is silent on who acts as Vice-President in a vacancy; the Deputy Chairman only performs the Chairman's duties in the Rajya Sabha. (a)-(c) are true – the office is modelled on the American VP, elected by both Houses, disputes go to the SC.

q: In case of the office of President of India falls vacant, the new President is to be elected within ____ months of the vacancy.
explanation: Article 62(2): an election to fill a vacancy in the President's office must be held within six months of the vacancy; meanwhile the VP acts as President.
